# The Workstation theme toggle flips instantly, with no reveal

## Context

The operator, exploring the Workstation before tomorrow's rehearsal: the Portal's theme button plays a growing-circle reveal from the pointer, and the Workstation's flips instantly. The reveal is not Portal-bespoke — it is an engine primitive with exactly one caller today.

**Live latest-open sweep:** checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-02T15:50Z; no equivalent found. `#18036` (document DockLayouts styling/themes) is documentation of a different surface; `#18107` is theme *sheet weight*, not the switch. **A2A in-flight sweep:** 14 most recent messages, all read-states — @neo-fable holds rail motion (`#18116` exit, `#18117` retarget, `#18122` maximize); none is the theme switch. **Own-assignment sweep:** six open, none on this surface. **Grep:** `resources/content/issues/` matches only `issue-17739.md`, the engine ticket that hardened the primitive — prior art, not a duplicate.

## The Problem

`Neo.main.DomAccess.startViewTransition()` already exists, is registered as a remote method, and is app-neutral. The Portal calls it in five lines and passes the click's raw coordinates so the engine owns the unit decision. The Workstation never calls it, so its one theme control is the only piece of chrome in the app that changes state without motion — next to a dock whose rails now slide in and out (`#18074`, `#18116`, `#18117`).

Verified before filing rather than assumed: `grep startViewTransition apps/workstation/` returns nothing, and the toggle's handler is `handler: () => me.toggleWorkspaceTheme()` — an arrow taking no arguments, calling a method taking none.

## The Architectural Reality

| surface | file:line | today |
|---|---|---|
| the engine primitive | `src/main/DomAccess.mjs:1082` | `startViewTransition({animate, delay, reveal, windowId})`; returns `false` with no View Transition API |
| the only caller | `apps/portal/view/ViewportController.mjs:285` | awaits the call, then `me.setTheme(newTheme)` inside the `delay` window |
| the Workstation button | `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:688` | `handler: () => me.toggleWorkspaceTheme()` — discards the event |
| the Workstation flip | `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:2618` | `toggleWorkspaceTheme()` → `setWorkspaceTheme(theme)`, no arguments |

**The scope asymmetry, stated because it is the reason this ticket is main-window-only.** `setWorkspaceTheme` deliberately fans across `Neo.appsByName[me.appName]` rather than the window-keyed registry, with a standing comment that iterating the latter "would let a Workstation toggle retheme an unrelated co-hosted app" — and it notes "one window today, one per open vessel tomorrow". But `document.startViewTransition()` captures the **whole document** and runs in **one** document. So:

- A co-hosted app would be swept by the reveal circle while its own colours do not change. Latent today — the Workstation is a single `name: 'Workstation'` app owning its document — but real if that changes.
- Once vessels are open, the main window reveals and the pop-outs flip instantly.

Neither is a defect introduced here; both are consequences of animating a document while theming an app. This ticket takes the main window because that is where the click happens, and records the vessel question rather than discovering it during a demo.

## The Fix

1. `Workspace.mjs:688` — `handler: data => me.toggleWorkspaceTheme(data)`, so the click survives.
2. `toggleWorkspaceTheme(data)` — await `Neo.main.DomAccess.startViewTransition({delay: 100, reveal: {x: data.clientX, y: data.clientY}, windowId: me.windowId})`, then apply the flip, matching the Portal's ordering exactly: the flip must land **inside** the `delay` window or the transition captures the unchanged DOM as both states.
3. No engine change. No new file. No SCSS.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

N/A — this ticket introduces no consumed surface. It adds a second caller to `Neo.main.DomAccess#startViewTransition()`, whose contract is already ledgered on `#17739`: resolves `true` once the transition has **started** (never once it has finished), `false` when the browser lacks the API, and reveal failure is reported asynchronously via `console.warn`. `toggleWorkspaceTheme()`'s return value changes from `String` to `Promise<String>`; its only caller is the button handler, and the tour/spec callers are checked in AC-5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — clicking the Workstation theme button plays the circular reveal from the pointer, in both directions, on the served app.
- [ ] **AC-2** — the flip is applied *after* the awaited call, inside the `delay` window, so both captured states differ. A reversed order silently degrades to a no-op reveal and must not ship.
- [ ] **AC-3** — with no View Transition API the theme still flips. The engine returns `false` and the flip runs regardless; today's behaviour is the floor, so the change cannot regress a browser that lacks the feature.
- [ ] **AC-4** — the reveal originates at the pointer, not at a fixed point. A missing `clientX/clientY` must not throw; `DomUtils.createRevealAnimation()` owns that fallback and is not reimplemented here.
- [ ] **AC-5** — every existing caller of `toggleWorkspaceTheme()` still works with the now-async signature: the tour screenplay and any spec that toggles the theme. Enumerated and checked, not assumed.
- [ ] **AC-6 (post-merge, real browser)** — read by eye. `startViewTransition` is unsupported in headless (recorded on `pr-13430`), so **no headless arm can witness AC-1**. Unit coverage asserts the call shape and ordering; the reveal itself is an operator/author read.

## Out of Scope

- **Vessel fan-out.** Pop-out windows keep flipping instantly. Revealing per vessel means fanning the engine call across windows, which is a separate decision with its own timing question (simultaneous or staggered), not a quick win.
- **The Portal's call site.** Untouched.
- **Any engine change to `DomAccess` or `DomUtils`.** If one turns out to be needed, that is a finding and a new ticket, not scope drift.
- **The co-hosted-document case**, which is latent and has no reproducer today.

## Avoided Traps

- **Reimplementing the reveal geometry in the app.** The Portal's comment says why: the App worker knows where the pointer was, not how a pseudo-element resolves a length. Passing raw coordinates keeps the unit decision in one engine place instead of one copy per app. A second copy here would be the "N sites, one idiom" anti-pattern.
- **Awaiting the transition to completion.** `#17739` establishes this is unsatisfiable without breaking the feature — `transition.ready` resolves only after both snapshots are taken, so awaiting it would apply the theme *after* capture and the transition would capture the unchanged DOM twice.
- **Writing a headless arm for the reveal.** It would pass while witnessing nothing, because the API is absent in that environment. AC-6 names the bound instead.

## Related

- `#17739` / PR `#17743` — hardened `startViewTransition()`; the contract this consumes.
- `#13158` — the QT-parity docking polish epic this sits beside.
- `#18116` / `#18117` — the rail motion work that makes the instant theme flip conspicuous.
- PR `#13430` — the archived note recording that the animated switch cannot be verified headless.
